transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Kim (Redwood AE), Rina Patel (Redwood SE), Omar Hassan (Redwood SA), Alex Chen (Meridian CTO), Priya Rao (Meridian Platform), Diego Morales (Meridian Sec), Samira N'diaye (Meridian Cloud Ops)

Summary (auto): Handoff of connector packaging and listing playbook. Focus on VPC/private control plane, KMS compatibility, helm/operator choices, and billing hooks for marketplace. Action items captured.

Transcript:
00:00 Jesse (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call and I'll hand it over to Rina to run the playbook walkthrough.
00:14 Alex Chen (Meridian): Hi, Alex here. We have Priya and Diego as well. Excited to see the pattern.
00:21 Rina (Redwood): Great, so the goal today is to run through the recommended packaging and the hybrid connector pattern—how you list in the marketplace but still keep inference in your VPC or on-prem. I'll show the helm chart structure, the operator options, and the KMS flow.
00:40 Priya (Meridian): Quick question on that—when you say "operator options" do you mean a full operator that manages model artifacts and kv cache or just a lightweight helm chart?
00:53 Rina (Redwood): Good call. We actually recommend two patterns: lightweight helm + kustomize for smaller installs; and a small operator for teams that want lifecycle hooks (model rollouts, canaries). The operator is optional; it adds reconciliation and makes rollouts consistent. Transcription note: we said "K V cache" a couple times, sometimes transcribed as separate letters.
01:18 Diego (Meridian): For security we need a clear KMS flow. Are you tying into our customer KMS or using Redwood-managed keys?
01:26 Omar (Redwood): We support both. For Private deployments you can bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) and we integrate via envelope encryption; for Dedicated/Hosted we offer Redwood KMS and can integrate with HSM for FIPS. There may be a little setup for key policies.
01:44 Diego: Ok, can you share what IAM roles or trust relationships we need for the connector to call the control plane?
01:50 Rina: Yep. We'll include an example IAM role with least-privilege policy in the repo. For hybrid the control plane is private by default; we support a private endpoint that you either peer to or use a gateway. We'll document both.
02:10 Samira (Meridian): On connectivity, what's your recommended pattern for latency-sensitive workloads? We don't want an extra 100-200 ms hop.
02:19 Jesse (Redwood): For low-latency we recommend local inference (on-prem or dedicated pools) with the connector handling tokenized requests and KV cache locally. When you need model updates or metrics, the connector batches telemetry. If you deploy in a cloud region close to clients and peer the VPC, typical added latency is sub-20 ms. But that's obviously workload dependent.
02:45 Priya: Does the playbook cover quantized model packaging? We do a lot of 8-bit and need guidance on model artifacts.
02:52 Rina: Yes, there's a model packaging section — we have patterns for storing multiple quantized variants and how the rollout hooks can swap artifacts. We'll include manifest examples for q4_0 and int8 variants. Note: sometimes the transcript changes model names slightly, e.g., "q 4" instead of q4.
03:14 Alex: From a marketplace perspective, how do billing hooks work? We want metering to align to our SKU model.
03:22 Omar: Marketplace integration uses event hooks. We offer a lightweight metering endpoint that emits token-level usage or inference-unit events. For marketplace SKUs we map usage lines to SKU IDs and emit billing events to the marketplace connector. We'll share a mapping template.
03:44 Alex: Any constraints on metering frequency or cost overhead?
03:49 Rina: Metering is batched every minute by default; overhead is minimal. If you need per-request metering we can support it but that increases cost. Also you can use sampling for logs to reduce egress.
04:10 Priya: There was a note about private control plane — does that mean the control plane is inside our VPC?
04:16 Omar: Two options: 1) Private control plane where Redwood runs a control plane stack deployed into your VPC (customer-managed control plane) or 2) A managed private endpoint where Redwood's control plane remains hosted but reachable only from your VPC via peering or private link. The first option gives more isolation but requires more ops.
04:40 Diego: For audits, we need full request logs for a two-week window and immutable audit trails. Can that be stored in our S3?
04:48 Rina: Yes, we can ship logs to your S3 or your SIEM. We support immutable write-once configs with object lock depending on provider. We'll include the log-forwarding pattern.
05:05 Alex: Ok let's talk UAT. What are the recommended acceptance criteria?
05:12 Jesse: We propose a short checklist: deploy helm chart into test VPC, run three workloads (small/medium/large), measure token throughput at 90th percentile, validate key rotation, run security checklist, and verify billing events. We'll send the formal UAT checklist.
05:35 Samira: Timeline—can we do UAT the week of Dec 13? That's when we have capacity.
05:41 Jesse: Yes that works. We'll aim to have playbook + benchmark script in your hands by Dec 6.
05:48 Priya: On the operator vs helm choice, are there any gotchas for K8s distributions? We run EKS and an internal on-prem k8s.
05:56 Rina: We test against EKS and vanilla k8s. The helm chart has conditional templates so the operator components are optional. For on-prem we'll include notes on storage classes for model artifacts and best practices for PV size.
06:14 Diego: Any concerns about node-GPU drivers or inferencing runtimes? We use mixed GPU fleet.
06:20 Omar: We'll provide a compatibility matrix. The runtime relies on standard CUDA & ROCm stacks; for certain micro-optimizations we recommend a specific driver window but it's not required. We'll list recommended driver versions and a lightweight smoke test.
06:42 Alex: Are there competitors or alternative patterns we should be aware of?
06:46 Jesse: Customers sometimes evaluate CloudVendorX's managed endpoints or ModelServeCo's on-prem operator; we highlighted cost/latency tradeoffs previously.
07:00 Priya: Ok, last question—what does the support handoff look like after listing? Who owns first-line support for integration issues?
07:09 Omar: Redwood will provide an SRE rotation for the first 30 days of pilot, and we can extend. For production we'll propose a joint-run model with defined escalation. We'll capture support SLAs in the SOW.
07:28 Alex: Great. Anything else?
07:31 Jesse: No, that's it. We'll capture the playbook PR and invite you to the channel.
07:36 Samira: Thanks everyone.

(End of meeting)
